A_target.statement:
Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a [[Definition:Bounded Real Sequence|bounded real sequence]].
Then $\displaystyle \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} a_n = \sup_n \inf_{k \mathop \ge n} a_k$ is the smallest [[Definition:Subsequential Limit|subsequential limit]] of $\sequence {a_n}$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a bounded real sequence.
Then $\displaystyle \limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} b_n = \inf_n \sup_{k \mathop \ge n} b_k$ is the largest subsequential limit of $\sequence {b_n}$.

object_map.reformulation: Negation reverses the order on R, exchanging suprema with infima and largest with smallest.

validity_conditions: Negation is an order-reversing bijection of R, which is all the argument uses.
Boundedness is needed for both quantities to be finite.
proof_plan:
Let $b_n = -a_n$.
Then $\displaystyle \inf_{k \mathop \ge n} a_k = -\sup_{k \mathop \ge n} b_k$.

Hence:
:$\displaystyle \sup_n \inf_{k \mathop \ge n} a_k = -\inf_n \sup_{k \mathop \ge n} b_k = -\limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} b_n$

$l$ is a subsequential limit of $\sequence {a_n}$ {{iff}} $-l$ is one of $\sequence {b_n}$.
As negation reverses order, the largest subsequential limit of $\sequence {b_n}$ corresponds to the smallest of $\sequence {a_n}$.

By the source result, $\displaystyle -\limsup b_n$ is therefore the smallest subsequential limit of $\sequence {a_n}$, and equals $\displaystyle \liminf a_n$.
{{qed}}
